references.text: Jesus' words that the sickness is not unto death but for God's glory directly prepare for the promise of seeing God's glory in this chapter.
Jesus expresses joy that they were not there, so that they may believe, and links this directly to seeing God's glory through the resurrection.
Jesus speaks of God's glory being revealed through his death and resurrection, a theme fulfilled in Lazarus' resurrection and preparing for Jesus' own.
In his solemn prayer, Jesus asks that the Father glorify the Son, so that the Son may glorify the Father, a mutual glory central to the promise of seeing God's glory.
The prophecy that all will see God's glory coincides with Jesus' promise that faith will lead to the sight of God's glory.
God's promise to show his glory to his people, so that they may know that He is the Lord, reflects Jesus' intention to reveal God's glory through a sign.
